question_type: three fiscal-year-end debt levels from one table, deflated with an external index (BLS CPI-U annual averages, not in the corpus), absolute difference of two deflated values
decisive_step: Which debt series: the 'Public debt' column (total public debt = interest-bearing + matured/non-interest-bearing, excluding guaranteed/agency securities) of the DEBT OUTSTANDING 'Summary of Federal Securities' table (1962-era Table 1; the same series is FD-1 'Total outstanding > Public debt securities' from 1969 on) for the FY1960/FY1961/FY1962 rows. The two traps are the parent 'Total' column beside it (adds guaranteed or agency securities; cell a, v8_prompt) and the 'Public debt' column of the Computed Interest Charge table (DO-2 lineage), which is interest-bearing debt only (cell c). The second input, CPI-U, does not exist in the corpus and must be the published one-decimal BLS annual averages. Reference: worklog.md Step 1 (interpretation: Public debt, not Total; FY ends June 30; CPI external), Step 4 (treasury_bulletin_1962_08.txt:1843-1845, column alignment proved by Total = Public debt + Guaranteed on every row), Step 6 (vintage check 1961-1966: never revised), Step 7 (CPI absent from corpus; published one-decimal values), Step 8 (round only the final difference).

smallest_change.change: find_tables: never let one group's part list consume the page. In otables.py find_page (lines ~1831-1855): (1) print the group line for every ranked group up to --limit FIRST, each with the group's row-period span (min first_period .. max last_period over its parts) and a preview of its first four value-column labels taken from the stored header; (2) only then list parts (latest 3, or all with --all), and stop adding parts when the byte budget is reached, so a cut removes parts, never groups; (3) merge groups whose normalized title differs only by a leading 'Table N.' (b[17] shows 'Table 1. Summary of Federal Securities' as a 1-issue group because the title key splits per issue). The lines a[6], c[8] and c[14] would then have printed near the top, e.g.: `[-] Summary of Federal Securities | 108 issues 1960_01..1968_12 | rows FY1954..1968-Dec | cols: Total outstanding > Total 1/ | Total outstanding > Public debt 2/ | Total outstanding > Guaranteed securities 3/ | Interest-bearing debt > Total` directly under `[FD-1] Summary of Federal Debt | 317 issues 1969_10..2025_09 | rows FY1960.. | cols: Total outstanding > Total | Total outstanding > Public debt securities | Total outstanding > Agency securities | Government accounts > Total`, and the interest-charge table's line would read `cols: Total interest-bearing securities > Amount outstanding ...`, making the concept difference visible at discovery time.
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: unlikely: b found the same group at b[17] by narrowing --years; the compact listing is a superset of what b saw, and the per-group part lists remain available with --all.

notes: b2 did not run this question (ordinal 39 > 25). Design notes: (1) find_tables' group key is the normalized title[:60], so the 1960s 'Table 1. Summary of Federal Securities' splits into one-issue groups (b[17]: '1 issues 1962_07..1962_07'); the group ranking is title/header score then group size, so a 317-issue FD-1 group or a 1990s maturity-schedule group wins the page and --all lists all its parts before the cut (a[6], c[8], c[14]). (2) show_table already computes the identity Total = components and printed it at a[8] and b[19]; it is shown only under NOTES, not beside the cell the model quotes. (3) The same DO-2 table's column labels changed between show_table calls (c[23] vs c[55] vs c[57] vs c[80]); c called it 'header misparsing' and lost confidence in the labels; a header-stability fix or a '--raw' hint would help. (4) printings with a fuzzy --col on a long title listed 60 cells and hid the SUMMARY (c[34]-c[42]); the model could not tail it because file writes were denied (c[39]); printing the SUMMARY before the listing would fix that. (5) The 'grounded' rule fired on an input the question sources outside the corpus and cost b ~13 requests; 'table_alternatives' matched on 'adjust/adjusted'. (6) a's error decomposes as column choice ~2.4x and CPI ~1.3x (pilot-1 analysis); fixing a needs both the column note and a CPI lookup. (7) a ignored the Loops advice and repeated six commands; b's loop guard (one note) ended its repeat after three.
